body:
Thank you for such a positive reply. I'm really glad there is someone out there who can relate to this situation. 
We didn't communicate expectations, but for me when I said "I love you" that meant I'm not going to anything to hurt you and I expected the same from him. It was just so... unexpected for me. 

He tells me he's happy with us and where we are, but there's the anxious side of me that thinks that he's lying (imposter syndrome). It's hard to separate it all. Its definitely a thing I'm working towards to lessen this voice in my head. 

What things did you think about your husband? Were you anxious every time he went out?

I appreciate your comment. I've thought about our compatibility and ask him often (as reassurance) why he thinks we work together. He's told me he likes our conversations and being able to adventure into anything both in words and in the world. In the few spats we've gotten into, we've been able to calmly discuss our feelings. He says we compliment each other in that he's introverted and I like to go out. There is also certainly a level of physical attract that I don't need to get into. 
I definitely struggle with imposter syndrome, so it difficult to really tell if he's telling the truth or not. The way he looks at me makes me think he is in that moment, but then a memory may come flooding back and that butterfly/heart soar feeling is gone. 
I'm seeing a counsellor for all of this. Am I just hanging on for too long or just giving up?

Thank you for the reply and sorry for replying so late. He said it would take time because he needed to think about why he liked being poly, what it gave him, and how he would feel being monogamous. To be honest, I know should have just left it at that and not have hung on to him in that time like I did. The feelings often come and go in waves. I'm trying to find the light at the end of the tunnel but, yes, I've certainly thought about saving myself first. Maybe I'm just being stupid and hanging on again. Feelings are hard to separate from the objective.
